chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about a man who slapped another man on his face, and the slap turned black.

He عليه السلام said: If the slap turns black, then for it there are six dinars; if it turns green, then for it there are three dinars; if it turns red, then for it there is one dinar and a half; and on the body, half of that.

key_terms.اللَّطْمَةُ: a slap-mark or visible trace left by a slap
key_terms.الْبَدَنِ: the body, as distinct from the face in assessing compensation
key_terms.ثَلَاثَةُ دَنَانِيرَ: three dinars as the compensation for greening of the face
key_terms.دِينَارٌ وَنِصْفٌ: one and a half dinars as the compensation for reddening of the face
key_terms.سِتَّةُ دَنَانِيرَ: six dinars as the compensation for blackening of the face

ai.seo_question: What is the compensation in Shia fiqh for a slap that leaves black, green, or red marks?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on financial compensation for a slap that leaves visible discoloration. It specifies different amounts according to the severity of the mark on the face, and states that comparable injuries on the body carry half the amount.
